title: Court of the Sealed Docket — proposal
open: Can a self-contained adjudicator decide a dispute on encrypted evidence without ever seeing that evidence in the clear, yet release a judgment together with authorized reasons and a certificate that agreed procedural rules were followed? The goal is a portable construction — an executable "court" — that takes sealed inputs and outputs only what the docket permits.
status: Currently a proposal; what is missing is a formal admissibility calculus and confidentiality guarantees under adaptive litigation. Related groundwork includes functional encryption and private, verifiable contracts in Raziel.
solved_when: A portable adjudicator exists that accepts encrypted evidence and releases exactly a judgment, authorized reasons, and a certificate of compliance with the agreed procedural rules, supported by a formal admissibility calculus and proven confidential even under adaptive litigation.
why: It would let trade-secret disputes and confidential arbitration run — and remain verifiable — even after the original operator disappears, since the adjudicator carries its own procedural authority.
key_works: Functional encryption; private, verifiable contracts in Raziel.

title: Counterfactual Equality Tribunal — proposal
open: Can a claimant demonstrate, through a verifiable counterfactual challenge, that an explicitly protected transformation of their record alters a confidential decision in a prohibited way — without exposing the underlying scoring system or record?
status: Currently a proposal; the missing pieces are defensible transformation rules and privacy bounds for repeated counterfactual challenges. Related foundations come from verifiable computation and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A tribunal procedure exists with defensible transformation rules and proven privacy bounds that hold under repeated counterfactual challenges, so that a claimant can obtain a verifiable answer while the scoring system and record remain confidential.
why: It would make rights of appeal against confidential scoring systems executable in practice, rather than merely declared on paper.
key_works: Verifiable computation and proof-carrying code.

title: Exculpation-Only Evidence Trust — proposal
open: Can protected evidence be made to release only exculpatory findings — that is, to authorize specifically favorable remedies while remaining provably useless to any adverse-evidence query? Formally, is there a scheme where a failed petition, or any combination of favorable findings, leaks nothing that an adversary-evidence interface could exploit?
status: Currently a proposal with no construction; the open need is a leakage analysis covering failed petitions and combinations of favorable findings. Related key work: function-specific disclosure through functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists together with a leakage analysis showing that failed petitions and arbitrary combinations of favorable findings reveal nothing usable through any adverse-evidence interface.
why: It would let confidential witnesses and institutional archives correct injustice without wholesale disclosure.
key_works: Function-specific disclosure through functional encryption.

title: Precedent Shadow Registry — proposal
open: Can a versioned institution, such as a court system, apply an agreed abstraction of sealed precedents while exposing only the resulting public doctrine and case outcome — never the underlying sealed judgments themselves?
status: This is currently a proposal, with no mechanism realized. The main known obstacles are that repeated outcomes may identify individual precedents, and the update and conflict rules for the versioned institution remain to be formalized. Candidate enabling tools are multi-input functional encryption and decentralized private computation.
solved_when: A formal mechanism exists in which the institution's outputs (public doctrine and case outcomes) reveal no more than an agreed abstraction of sealed judgments, repeated outcomes cannot be traced back to identify individual precedents, and the update and conflict rules are fully formalized.
why: It would allow consistent adjudication that draws on private settlements and sealed precedents without maintaining a permanent archive-reading judicial elite with privileged access to the raw record.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and decentralized private computation.

title: Anonymous Remedy Court — proposal
open: Can a claimant prove eligibility for a remedy and receive an enforceable payment or service right while remaining unlinkable across all stages — that is, without any party being able to connect the proof of eligibility, the claim itself, and the eventual payout to a single identity?
status: This is a proposal stage problem; no construction is known. The stated obstacle is that eligibility evidence, duplicate claims, and payment metadata must compose without reconstructing identities. Key works: anonymous credentials and Zexe's private asset machinery.
solved_when: A construction exists in which eligibility evidence, duplicate-claim prevention, and payment metadata compose end-to-end without reconstructing identities, and the resulting payment or service right is enforceable against the issuing institution.
why: It would enable redress systems for stigmatized injuries and confidential institutional failures, where claimants today face the choice between obtaining a remedy and exposing themselves.
key_works: Anonymous credentials and Zexe’s private asset machinery.

title: Minimum-Disclosure Reasons Bureau — proposal
open: Can an adjudicator publish a reason for a ruling that is independently checkable yet discloses nothing beyond itself — a justification drawn from an agreed explanation language, accompanied by a certificate that no shorter justification in that language exists?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The core obstacles are that minimality can be computationally expensive to establish and that the choice of explanation itself can leak information. Related foundations come from proof-carrying code and zero-knowledge verifiable computation.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the adjudicator outputs both a checkable explanation from the agreed language and an irreducibility (minimality) certificate, such that appeals can be resolved with useful reasons while unrelated secrets are preserved.
why: It would let courts and executable-justice systems give meaningful, appealable justifications without leaking information unrelated to the case at hand.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and zero-knowledge verifiable computation.

title: Recusal Without Accusation — proposal
open: Can a panel-selection institution publicly certify that its chosen members satisfy a published conflict-of-interest policy over confidential relationship records, without anyone learning the underlying relationships? Formally, this asks for a scheme in which the institution proves policy compliance over encrypted or hidden inputs, so that no central readable map of professional and family ties is ever formed.
status: Currently only a proposal; no construction exists. The open problems are that undeclared relationships remain outside the model, and repeated exclusions can expose hidden connections. Multi-input functional encryption is the key technique identified as relevant.
solved_when: A construction exists in which conflict screening is performed over confidential relationship records such that undeclared relationships remain hidden from all parties, and the process leaks no information enabling discovery of hidden connections through repeated exclusions.
why: It enables conflict screening without creating a central readable map of professional and family ties — today's screening either requires disclosure or risks exposing hidden connections through repeated exclusions.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption.

title: Witness-Refinement Appeals Chamber — proposal
open: Can an appeals mechanism be designed so that any revised judgment is attributable entirely to newly admitted evidence or an explicitly authorized correction, with no drift in the institution's decision criteria? Formally, is there an appeal interface for which the revised judgment is a provable function of (old record, new evidence, authorized corrections) alone?
status: This is a proposal; the appeal interface currently needs a theorem preventing materiality tests from becoming an evidence-extraction oracle. Key works referenced: functional encryption and verifiable computation.
solved_when: A revised judgment can be shown to result solely from newly admitted evidence or an explicitly authorized correction — specifically, via a theorem showing that materiality tests in the appeal interface cannot serve as an evidence-extraction oracle.
why: It enables reconsideration of decisions without letting an institution quietly move its decision criteria under the guise of review.
key_works: Functional encryption and verifiable computation.

title: Constitution With a Sealed Administrative Interior — proposal
open: Can an institution publish and prove the correctness of a constitutional envelope — a public guarantee that every recognized action it takes respects stated limits — while keeping its designated allocation parameters sealed from public view?
status: Currently a proposal; no construction exists. Rights need precise semantics, and cryptographic consistency alone cannot establish political legitimacy. Related directions include proof-carrying code and hidden mechanism design.
solved_when: A formal construction exists in which a designated set of allocation parameters remains confidential, yet any recognized action is accompanied by a publicly verifiable proof that it lies within the public constitutional envelope, with precise semantics for the rights the envelope encodes.
why: It would allow administrations to keep operational details confidential while their discretion is cryptographically constrained, so secrecy could no longer serve as cover for exceeding public authority.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and hidden mechanism design.

title: Amendment Admission Corridor — proposal
open: Can an institution be given a constitution that permits legitimate amendment while provably barring hostile change — admitting a proposed amendment only if it preserves designated protected rights and satisfies a confidential transition policy that was committed to before any proposal was seen?
status: This is currently a proposal only. The central identified obstacle is that hostile amendment proposals act as an adaptive oracle against the hidden compatibility policy. Related machinery includes Raziel's proof certificates and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A mechanism exists for which amendment admission is demonstrably governed by the hidden, previously committed compatibility policy: legitimate amendments satisfying the protected rights and transition policy are admitted, while hostile proposals — even those adaptively probing the mechanism as an oracle — are rejected.
why: It would let institutions evolve their rules over time without relying on unrestricted administrator upgrade keys, removing a single point of trusted authority.
key_works: Raziel’s proof certificates and proof-carrying code.

title: Nonretroactivity Engine — proposal
open: Can we construct an engine in which a properly registered historical event remains permanently evaluated under the constitutional version in force at its registration, so that no later constitutional revision can swap in a different evaluator? Formally, this asks for nonretroactivity: the evaluation function bound to a past event must be immutable under all subsequent version changes.
status: The proposal is currently a construction target without an existing implementation; the record notes that event timing and cross-system registration need trustworthy provenance and explicit dispute procedures. Related machinery comes from versioned commitments and private state transitions in Zexe.
solved_when: A registered event's evaluator is provably invariant across all later constitutional versions, with trustworthy provenance for event timing and cross-system registration plus explicit dispute procedures resolving any challenge to which version applies.
why: It would give digital institutions enforceable protection against retrospective rule substitution — no authority could rejudge past actions under newly minted rules.
key_works: Versioned commitments and private state transitions in Zexe.

title: Minority Veto Without a Membership List — proposal
open: Can a defined class of credential holders jointly block a specified action while revealing nothing beyond the fact that the veto threshold was satisfied — in particular, without any membership list being revealed or maintained?
status: This is a proposal with no known construction; credential issuance and coalition privacy still require explicit assumptions, and public outcomes continue to reveal that collective action occurred. Related technical machinery comes from anonymous credentials and constrained pseudorandom functions.
solved_when: A construction is given in which (i) only holders of credentials from the defined class can participate, (ii) the veto takes effect exactly when the threshold is met, and (iii) an observer learns only that the threshold was satisfied, not which members participated or who belongs to the class, under explicitly stated assumptions for credential issuance and coalition privacy.
why: It would give enforceable minority protections inside organizations where disclosure of membership carries real costs, something current governance mechanisms cannot offer.
key_works: Anonymous credentials and constrained pseudorandom functions.

title: Secret Emergency Fuse — proposal
open: Can an institution commit publicly to hard limits on an emergency response — its maximum scope, duration, and expenditure — while keeping the specific detection parameters that trigger the response secret? Formally, this asks for a mechanism whose activation conditions are private (e.g., via functional-encryption-style obfuscation) yet whose every execution provably stays within a publicly fixed envelope.
status: Currently a proposal only. The approach draws on functional encryption and proof-carrying code; it requires reliable event sources and a proof that every activation path obeys the public envelope, which are not yet established.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the designated detection parameters remain private, the scope, duration, and expenditure of any emergency response are publicly fixed in advance, and there is a proof that every activation path obeys that public envelope, with reliable event sources for triggering.
why: It would allow genuine emergency preparedness without publishing every operational trigger, so adversaries cannot game the disclosed thresholds while the public still retains verifiable guarantees that any response is bounded.
key_works: Functional encryption and proof-carrying code.

title: Jurisdiction Mutex — proposal
open: Can a cross-jurisdiction dispute yield at most one validly adjudicating authority, even when jurisdictions apply a shared priority rule? Formally, is there a mechanism under which the priority rule, together with a mutually recognized registry, precludes simultaneous incompatible adjudications of the same dispute?
status: The proposal observes that participating jurisdictions must recognize the same registry and specify how contested facts enter it; no mechanism achieving the mutex guarantee is currently known. Related foundations come from work on hidden mechanisms and ledger-based private computation.
solved_when: A mechanism is exhibited in which participating jurisdictions recognize the same registry, specify how contested facts enter it, and the shared priority rule guarantees that at most one valid adjudication authority can arise for any single dispute.
why: It would let cross-institution agreements avoid silently authorizing incompatible proceedings, which is the failure mode such agreements must rule out.
key_works: Hidden mechanisms and ledger-based private computation.

title: Schism-Conserving Charter — proposal
open: Can an organization pre-commit to a confidential rule that, upon a schism, distributes its recognized assets, duties, and capabilities among the successor institutions in a way that remains enforceable? Formally, this asks for a "schism-conserving charter": an allocation rule fixed in advance whose execution conserves obligations and entitlements even as the institution splits.
status: This is a proposal. No construction exists; the outstanding obstacles identified are that off-registry assets and obligations need external enforcement, and that private allocation rules require adaptive confidentiality analysis.
solved_when: A construction exists for a preagreed confidential fission rule that provably distributes all recognized assets, duties, and capabilities among successor institutions, and whose enforcement is shown to hold under adaptive confidentiality analysis even when off-registry assets and obligations require external enforcement.
why: It enables peaceful organizational separation whose mechanics remain enforceable during a governance breakdown, rather than collapsing into contestation over undisclosed assets and duties.
key_works: Zexe and Hawk.

title: Counterexample Sovereignty — proposal
open: Can a system be designed so that a valid counterexample to a registered invariant automatically triggers a bounded remedy, without any administrator needing to consent? Formally: what mechanisms make counterexample-triggered enforcement sovereign, i.e., executable without discretionary approval?
status: Currently a proposal, unsolved; the obstacles are the need for useful formal invariants, complete challenge interfaces, and remedies that cannot create new violations. Related foundations come from proof-carrying code and publicly verifiable computation.
solved_when: A construction exists in which any valid counterexample to a registered invariant produces a bounded remedy automatically, where the invariants are formally useful, the challenge interface is complete, and remedies provably cannot create new violations.
why: It would make constitutional promises backed by executable challenge rights rather than discretionary enforcement.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and publicly verifiable computation.

title: Self-Negotiating Use Right — proposal
open: Can a software entitlement negotiate its own licensing terms — carrying a private reservation schedule over price, scope, duration, and permitted outputs — so that counterparties learn nothing beyond the agreed terms?
status: Repeated bargaining can expose reservation values; prospective rights need an authoritative registry. Proposed building blocks are hidden mechanism design and iO punctured programs.
solved_when: A construction exists in which an entitlement enforces its reservation schedule through repeated bargaining without exposing the schedule itself, backed by an authoritative registry for prospective rights.
why: It would let intellectual assets transact without an always-available licensing intermediary.
key_works: Hidden mechanism design and iO punctured programs.

title: Divisible Computational Estate — proposal
open: Can an entitlement to run a computation be split into independent child rights, each governing a disjoint input class, output resolution, or recognized application domain, such that no combination of the children recovers the parent's full power?
status: Currently only a proposal; constrained pseudorandom functions and functional encryption are the key works grounding the idea, but no rights algebra or non-recombination proof yet exists.
solved_when: A tractable rights algebra is given for carving such entitlements, together with a proof that child capabilities cannot recombine into unauthorized powers.
why: It would enable markets in precisely carved computational rights, letting parties buy and sell exactly the slices of a computation they need.
key_works: Constrained pseudorandom functions and functional encryption.

title: Duty-Preserving Resale — proposal
open: When an executable program is resold, can the transfer carry along the seller's confidential royalty splits, support commitments, and specified onward-transfer conditions so that the buyer's copy still honors them? Formally: define a resale mechanism such that these duties are preserved and machine-checkable even though they bind parties off the underlying system.
status: Currently a proposal only. Known obstacles: duties binding parties off-system appear to require attestations, and the seller's old knowledge and copies cannot be erased. Related machinery includes Hawk and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A construction is given in which every resale of a program preserves confidential royalty splits, all support commitments, and any specified onward-transfer conditions, with off-system duties discharged via attestations and no dependence on erasing the seller's prior knowledge or copies.
why: It would enable secondary markets in executable intellectual property where obligations remain machine-checkable rather than merely contractual.
key_works: Hawk and proof-carrying code.

title: Capability Divorce — proposal
open: Can a jointly controlled service be split into successor rights that each party can use independently, so that no party retains leverage over the others after separation? Formally, is there a separation procedure that partitions a capability over such a service into independently usable successor capabilities with provable security even when those successors are correlated?
status: This is a proposal; no construction exists yet. What is missing is a security theorem for correlated successor capabilities and a clear treatment of already disclosed information. Related machinery comes from functional encryption and constrained delegation.
solved_when: A separation procedure exists together with a security theorem covering correlated successor capabilities and a clear treatment of information already disclosed before the separation.
why: It would let partnerships that share proprietary models, archives, or technical methods dissolve cleanly, without either party holding residual control over the other's continued use.
key_works: Functional encryption and constrained delegation.

title: Alienable Exception License — proposal
open: Can we construct a transferable license whose holder may exercise one defined exception without learning the confidential reason it was granted — that is, a credential whose use reveals only the sanctioned act, never the policy behind it?
status: This is a proposal. Successful use of such a license is known to reveal some policy information, so the target is to keep transfer and redemption unlinkable wherever that is promised. Candidate machinery includes Zexe's private rights machinery and functional encryption.
solved_when: A holder can redeem exactly one defined exception, transfer the license to another party, and neither redemption nor transfer is linkable to the original grant, beyond whatever policy information successful use is permitted to reveal.
why: It would enable negotiable waivers and special permissions that carry confidential background agreements, letting rights be traded and exercised without exposing why they were granted.
key_works: Zexe’s private rights machinery and functional encryption.

title: Sealed First-Refusal Deed — proposal
open: Can a program that holds a sealed "first-refusal" right over an asset respond correctly when a genuine external offer arrives — comparing confidentially and then either matching the purchase or issuing a release certificate?
status: The main obstacles are fabricated offers and repeated probing; a solution appears to require authentication, economic constraints, and a bargaining-leakage model. Related ideas appear in work on hidden mechanisms and Hawk.
solved_when: A genuine external offer triggers a confidential comparison whose outcome is verifiably either a matching purchase or a release certificate.
why: It would give autonomous priority rights over intellectual assets and shared infrastructure, so that claims can be exercised without exposing the negotiating party.
key_works: Hidden mechanisms and Hawk.

title: Computational Usufruct — proposal
open: Can we build a cryptographic scheme in which one party is entitled to specified future outputs or revenue of a computation, while a different party retains the authority to amend or transfer those rights — and prove the division of power holds under composition?
status: Currently a proposal; no construction or proof exists. The needed tools plausibly draw on functional encryption and constrained capabilities.
solved_when: A formal construction exists with a compositional separation-of-powers theorem, together with a dependable accounting mechanism that correctly attributes recognized sales of outputs.
why: It would enable trusts, endowments, and investment structures built around divided computational interests, where entitlement to a program's future value must coexist with someone else's managerial control.
key_works: Functional encryption and constrained capabilities.

title: Rights That Open Over Time — proposal
open: Can a program's access rights be made to widen automatically over time, so that authenticated milestones unlock new uses while never revoking rights already granted by the schedule?
status: Currently only a proposal: milestone authenticity and long-term migration need specification, and source disclosure needs a separate release-security argument. Related primitives are constrained functions and timed-release cryptography.
solved_when: A specification exists for milestone authenticity and long-term migration in such programs, together with a separate release-security argument for source disclosure, where authenticated milestones can expand access but provably cannot reduce rights already granted.
why: It would enable automatically maturing commons and research tools that gradually become broadly usable without a trusted party re-issuing permissions.
key_works: Constrained functions and timed-release cryptography.

title: Sealed-Covenant Rollup — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can a rollup be built in which anyone can publicly execute a published capsule and verify its accepted state transitions, without ever receiving the readable source logic or private state behind it? A formalization should achieve policy-confidentiality — hiding the contract logic while preserving public verifiability of execution.
status: This is currently a proposal. It still requires a concrete policy-confidentiality reduction and an explicit treatment of observable transaction patterns. Related key works include Hawk and Zexe.
solved_when: A concrete construction is given with a formal reduction establishing policy-confidentiality, together with an explicit analysis of observable transaction patterns; executing and verifying a capsule's accepted transitions must require no access to source logic or private state.
why: It would provide public execution infrastructure for confidential institutional agreements, where agreement logic and state must stay sealed even from the parties verifying execution.
key_works: Hawk and Zexe.

title: Auction House Without an Auctioneer — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can an auction be run so that a finalized roster of sealed bids deterministically yields a winning bidder, while the mechanism's logic — including its incentive and eligibility rules — remains confidential yet publicly precommitted? The goal is a construction in which the winner is selected by a precommitted secret mechanism whose published constraints are provably satisfied without any party reading the bids.
status: Bid inclusion, abort handling, and the precise incentive certificate remain separate design obligations. The proposal builds toward hidden mechanisms in the sense of Canetti–Fiat–Gonczarowski.
solved_when: A construction is given that takes a finalized bid roster and outputs a winner under a precommitted confidential mechanism satisfying the published incentive and eligibility constraints, together with handling of bid inclusion and abort behavior and a precise incentive certificate.
why: It would enable procurement and allocation processes that require no bid-reading intermediary, removing the need to trust any party with confidential bid data.
key_works: Canetti–Fiat–Gonczarowski’s hidden mechanisms.

title: Contract Federation With a Hidden Call Graph — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can a federation of contracts execute on shared infrastructure so that the authorized final effects of every agreement are publicly verifiable, while designated internal invocation relationships — which contract calls which, and when — remain hidden from all observers?
status: This is a proposal; no construction or theorem exists yet. What is needed is a compositional leakage theorem covering traffic, timing, storage access, and module correlations. Related foundational techniques include Path ORAM and Zexe.
solved_when: A compositional leakage theorem exists that bounds what any observer can learn from traffic, timing, storage access, and module correlations, and a construction realizes hidden-call-graph contract federation meeting that bound.
why: It would enable confidential supply-chain and consortium agreements to run on shared infrastructure without exposing which parties' contracts interact internally.
key_works: Path ORAM and Zexe.

title: Contingency Web — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can parties execute complex contingent agreements on-chain while keeping the contract's underlying logic hidden — that is, have a sealed graph of obligations that activates only selected settlements when authenticated events satisfy its private conditions?
status: This is a proposal with no known construction. Existing private-contract approaches such as Hawk's private contracts and functional encryption offer partial tools, but settlement correlations may reveal dormant clauses, and event attestations remain an external trust boundary.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the full graph of contingent obligations remains secret, only triggered settlements execute, and no settlement correlations reveal dormant clauses.
why: It would let parties enter complex contingent partnerships without exposing the entire map of possible deals, which today deters such arrangements.
key_works: Hawk’s private contracts and functional encryption.

title: Machine Warranty That Adjudicates Itself — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can a machine trigger its own warranty payout — authenticated operational evidence causes compensation under a diagnostic rule the provider committed to in advance, with no claims operator free to reinterpret or refuse it?
status: A proposal only; no construction exists. Sensor integrity, diagnostic validity, and controlled claim probing still need independent treatment. Related primitives come from verifiable computation and private smart contracts.
solved_when: A construction exists in which verifiable sensor/operational evidence, evaluated against a committed private contract, deterministically adjudicates and executes compensation, with sensor integrity, diagnostic validity, and resistance to controlled claim probing each treated independently.
why: It yields warranties that remain usable after the original claims department vanishes, removing dependence on a counterparty's continued goodwill.
key_works: Verifiable computation and private smart contracts.

title: Market for Composable Secret Clauses — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can independently developed secret clauses — modules that publish an interface contract and their proof obligations while hiding their implementation — be securely composed and traded, so that security survives the very linkage language permitted between them?
status: Independently secure modules can leak information through interaction; the missing result is a proof of security under the permitted linkage language. Related foundations come from proof-carrying code and Raziel.
solved_when: A formal treatment exists showing that independently secure clauses remain secure under all linkages expressible in the permitted composition language, with each clause still exposing only its public interface contract and proof obligations while its implementation stays protected.
why: It would enable a reusable market in proprietary contractual machinery, where vendors can sell clauses without disclosing their internal logic.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and Raziel.

title: Failure-Triggered Upgrade Corridor — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can a smart contract be designed so that a narrow, restricted migration path automatically becomes available only when a counterexample proves the contract violates an agreed operational invariant? Formally, define defect classes and a mechanism by which a verified violation certificate unlocks a bounded upgrade corridor from the original program to a repair or successor program, with no other escalation possible.
status: Currently a proposal; open problems include formalizing the defect classes and achieving secure composition among the original, repair, and successor programs. Key works: Raziel's certificates and Zexe's state-transition proofs.
solved_when: A formal taxonomy of defect classes is given, together with a secure composition scheme among the original, repair, and successor programs, such that the migration corridor opens exactly upon presentation of a valid counterexample certificate and grants only narrowly bounded emergency authority.
why: It would enable repairable contracts whose emergency powers are narrowly bounded by cryptographic proof, preventing both unfixable broken contracts and unlimited governance backdoors.
key_works: Raziel’s certificates and Zexe’s state-transition proofs.

title: Execution After Ordering — proposal
subfield: Public execution with secret contract logic
open: Can we construct a contract system in which a contract's actionable outputs become available only once a finalized batch of committed requests has been ordered — that is, no party, privileged or otherwise, can preview pending actions before execution order is fixed?
status: Ordering fairness, censorship, delivery timing, and external arbitrage remain outside iO's guarantee. Related efforts include Hawk and work on decentralized private computation.
solved_when: A realized protocol (e.g., via indistinguishability obfuscation of contract logic) in which a contract's outputs are released only for a finalized batch of committed requests, so that preview of pending actions is impossible before finalization.
why: It enables markets with less protocol-enabled preview of pending actions, closing off the information advantage that early visibility of uncommitted transactions currently grants.
key_works: Hawk and decentralized private computation.

title: Unborn-Strategy Treasury — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can an institution be constructed in which no participant gains privileged access to strategy information generated inside the protocol before its authorized execution?
status: Current understanding is that outside knowledge cannot be abolished, so the target is limited to unbiased distributed compilation and protected order delivery. Related work includes Dark DAO research and punctured programs.
solved_when: A protocol is achieved that provides unbiased distributed compilation and protected order delivery, given that outside knowledge cannot be abolished.
why: It would yield a precise form of insider-resistant, secret-strategy organization — a secret organization whose own members cannot front-run its strategies.
key_works: Dark DAO research and punctured programs.

title: Sealed Acquisition Cooperative — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can a cooperative of members with private valuations jointly produce authorized bids through a sealed acquisition process, such that nothing is revealed beyond the selected transaction and permitted accounting?
status: Currently, negotiation transcripts and observable purchases leak information about member valuations, and contribution completeness remains unresolved because no membership process has been defined. Related tools come from multi-input functional encryption.
solved_when: A mechanism exists that outputs authorized bids from private member valuations while leaking only the selected transaction and the permitted accounting, with a defined membership process ensuring contribution completeness.
why: It would enable collective purchasing in which the operator cannot assemble and sell a readable dossier of members' strategies.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption.

title: Fiduciary Without a Portfolio Reader — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can a treasury capsule reallocate its encrypted holdings while proving, to outside verifiers, compliance with explicit concentration, liquidity, and counterparty limits — without granting any party privileged access to read the underlying portfolio?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. Related directions include Raziel's private investment-fund direction and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the capsule provably enforces the declared concentration, liquidity, and counterparty limits on every reallocation, with asset attestations and cross-market settlement completing within the declared account universe.
why: It would enable custody and execution arrangements in which no participant — not even the custodian or executor — enjoys privileged preview of portfolio internals.
key_works: Raziel’s private investment-fund direction and proof-carrying code.

title: Equal-View Investment Gate — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can a multi-party institution be designed so that, during a designated disclosure window, no class of participants receives a richer authorized view of its internal state than any other? Formally, the construction must satisfy an equal-view gate: the authorized disclosure available to each participant class is information-equivalent across classes for the duration of the window.
status: This is currently a proposal. Achieving it requires an interface-completeness argument; it explicitly does not equalize outside information or network latency. Related key works are functional encryption and private broadcast encryption.
solved_when: A construction (with supporting analysis) exists in which every participant class's authorized disclosure about the institution's internal state during the window is provably equal in richness, verified via an interface-completeness argument; the design need not equalize outside information or network latency.
why: It would enable offerings with an auditable absence of privileged internal reporting channels, giving all participants verifiable assurance that no insider class holds an informational edge.
key_works: Functional encryption and private broadcast encryption.

title: Chairless Agenda — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can an organization run an agenda-selection process in which a committed rule selects and schedules submitted proposals, yet each item stays hidden until its authorized stage — so that no party, including whoever runs the mechanism, can preview or steer the outcome in advance? Formally, this asks for a scheduling mechanism whose selection function is fixed by a public commitment while individual agenda items remain private until release.
status: Framed as an open proposal drawing on randomized functional encryption and hidden mechanisms; no construction exists, and the needed guarantees against starvation, submission manipulation, and timing-based inference have not been established.
solved_when: A mechanism exists that selects and schedules proposals under a committed rule, reveals each item only at its authorized stage, and carries explicit guarantees against starvation, submission manipulation, and inference from release timing.
why: It would let institutions schedule decisions without a human gatekeeper who could privately sell preview or preferential placement of agenda items.
key_works: Randomized functional encryption and hidden mechanisms.

title: Procurement Office With Provable Constraints — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can a procurement office be run "sealed," so that no operator can rig or preview outcomes, while bidders still get verifiable assurance that the rules they bid under — public price formation, eligibility, conflict-of-interest, and award-consistency predicates — were actually honored? Formally, this asks for a mechanism whose constraints are provably enforced by cryptographic certification rather than by trust in the operator.
status: This is a proposal-stage problem. Current understanding is that hidden scoring does not eliminate collusion, and that certification must expose the properties bidders actually need to assess. Related work falls under hidden mechanism design.
solved_when: A construction exists for a reusable procurement office in which public price, eligibility, conflict, and award-consistency predicates are all enforced and certified, with operator discretion limited accordingly, and hidden scoring alone does not suffice — the certification must expose the properties bidders actually need to assess.
why: It would enable reusable procurement offices with limited operator discretion, removing the reliance on trusted hidden scoring that fails to eliminate collusion.
key_works: Hidden mechanism design.

title: Mutual-Loss Pact — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can a consortium of institutions jointly provide mutual assistance whenever their confidential aggregate stress function crosses a committed threshold, without any member revealing its detailed positions or gaining privileged preview of others' inputs? Formally: a protocol that combines multi-input functional encryption with strategic-reporting robustness so the trigger and the payout are both executable and privacy-preserving.
status: This is currently a proposal; exposure omissions, strategic reporting, and repeated threshold observations still need explicit models. Key works referenced are multi-input functional encryption and Hawk.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the aggregate stress function is evaluated confidentially against the committed threshold, agreed assistance is paid when the threshold is crossed, and explicit models handle exposure omissions, strategic reporting, and repeated threshold observations.
why: It would make mutual insurance among institutions executable in practice, letting them share risk without disclosing the detailed positions that make such pacts impossible today.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and Hawk.

title: Strategy Collision Observatory — proposal
subfield: Secret organizations and resistance to privileged preview
open: Can a group of mutually distrustful programs jointly learn whether their contemplated actions collide — that is, violate an agreed joint constraint — without any of them revealing its individual plan? Formally, this asks for a protocol computing the predicate "do the private strategies jointly violate the constraint?" under privacy of each input.
status: Open as a proposal; what is missing is a composition theorem for repeated correlated plans and incentives for complete participation. Multi-input functional encryption is identified as a key relevant technique.
solved_when: A protocol exists that (i) reveals only whether the joint constraint is violated, nothing about individual plans, and (ii) comes with a composition theorem covering repeated executions with correlated plans, together with incentives ensuring complete participation.
why: It would let confidential autonomous organizations coordinate against synchronized failures — detecting collisions before they happen — without surrendering the secrecy of their internal strategies.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption.

title: Executable Will — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: How can a "testamentary program" — an executable left behind like a will — be specified so that it grants future beneficiaries exactly the advisory, archival, or operational functions the deceased intended, and no more, even as the executing environment changes over time?
status: The problem is at the proposal stage. It is known that succession evidence, changing identities, and long-term cryptographic migration require durable rules; candidate building blocks are functional encryption and anonymous credentials, but no definition or construction of testamentary programs exists yet.
solved_when: A formal notion of a testamentary program exists, together with a construction realizing it, with rules durable enough to handle succession evidence, changing identities of beneficiaries, and long-term cryptographic migration (e.g., algorithm/credential upgrades over the program's lifetime) without breaking the intended access grants.
why: Estates increasingly contain computational expertise and private archives whose selective disclosure and continued operation have value; without durable rules, such assets are lost, leaked, or frozen when their owner dies or the surrounding infrastructure migrates.
key_works: Functional encryption and anonymous credentials.

title: Competence Escrow — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can we design a qualification process for institutional succession — a "competence escrow" — such that a future steward is granted registered authority only after demonstrating, through externally assessable means, the competence needed to wield it?
status: This is a proposal; no scheme exists yet. The central obstacle is that competence certificates require meaningful assessments, while proxy performance and colluding assessors remain possible.
solved_when: A scheme exists in which authority transfer occurs if and only if the steward completes a committed, externally assessable qualification process whose assessments are meaningful (resistant to proxy performance and colluding assessors).
why: It provides continuity for specialized institutions whose original experts disappear, so that critical authority and capabilities do not lapse with them.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and constrained capabilities.

title: Orphaned-Software Receiver — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can software be given a contractual "dead-man's switch" that automatically transfers continued-function capability to a receiver when the original vendor's obligations go unmet — without ever exposing the vendor's unrelated secrets? Formally, missed registered obligations should trigger activation of a precommitted fallback capability whose disclosure is limited to exactly the orphaned software's continuing function.
status: This is a proposal-stage problem; no construction or partial results are recorded. The known design constraint is that failure evidence, state availability, and continuing access to external dependencies must be contractually precise. Candidate building blocks are token-based obfuscation and reusable garbled circuits.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which failure evidence, state availability, and continuing access to external dependencies are contractually precise, such that a missed registered obligation deterministically activates the precommitted fallback while unrelated vendor secrets remain protected.
why: It would guarantee software continuity without depending on a source-code escrow agent being able to read (or be trusted with) the escrowed material.
key_works: Token-based obfuscation and reusable garbled circuits.

title: Surgical Patch Trust — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can a committed program be surgically repaired in place, so that a designated failure is provably removed while selected interfaces are provably preserved? Formally, the goal is a repair capability that transforms a committed program while carrying a proof both of interface preservation and of elimination of the specified failure.
status: This is a proposal-stage problem; no construction is known. The main identified tension is that the old and new behavior may themselves reveal the vulnerability being repaired, and related-program confidentiality therefore requires analysis. Key works: proof-carrying code and verifiable computation.
solved_when: A construction exists that transforms a committed program and produces verifiable evidence of (i) preservation of the selected interfaces and (ii) removal of the specified failure, without exposing information beyond what old and new behavior already reveal.
why: It would enable confidential maintenance arrangements — repairs by parties other than the original developer — that keep working as institutions and developers disappear, so long-lived software can be trusted without trusting its provenance.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and verifiable computation.

title: Theorem-Triggered Research Estate — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can a long-lived research endowment hold assets in escrow and release them exactly when some future mathematical or technical breakthrough occurs — that is, when a witness satisfying a fixed, efficiently checkable mathematical relation is presented?
status: Ordinary witness encryption protects false instances; secrecy for true instances with unknown witnesses needs a stronger assumption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a sealed research asset provably releases a specified function upon presentation of a witness satisfying the fixed checkable relation, and remains sealed otherwise.
why: It would let funding and resources respond autonomously to breakthroughs, without a trusted custodian deciding when a theorem has been proven.
key_works: Witness encryption and extractable timed-release constructions.

title: Perpetual Obligation Executor — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can a funded executable continue carrying out its specified payments, disclosures, and service obligations after the institution that created it ceases to operate — that is, survive as a self-sustaining program through institutional failure?
status: No construction exists; the proposal is at the stage of identifying obstacles. It is noted that "perpetual" operation requires sustainable funding, available data, and a migration process for obsolete cryptography. Key works: Hawk and decentralized private computation.
solved_when: A construction is exhibited in which an executable, backed by sustainable funding, continues performing its specified payments, disclosures, and service obligations after originating-institution shutdown, with available data access and a working migration process for obsolete cryptography.
why: It would make support promises and public-benefit commitments durable beyond the lifetime of the institution that issued them.
key_works: Hawk and decentralized private computation.

title: Collective Source Buyout Vault — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can a vault hold a source package such that it is released only when an authenticated funding-and-settlement condition is met, with the release guarantee holding even against adversarial participants? In other words: a construction, with a release-security reduction, that commits an escrowed package to publication exactly upon collective buyout.
status: Currently a proposal only. What remains open are a release-security reduction, a package-completeness proof, and a treatment of payment finality and delivery failure; related machinery exists in witness-conditioned release and private smart contracts.
solved_when: A construction is given with (i) a release-security reduction showing the package is released if and only if the authenticated funding and settlement condition is satisfied, (ii) a package-completeness proof that what is released is the full committed source package, and (iii) an explicit treatment of payment finality and delivery failure.
why: It would enable crowdfunded liberation of abandoned or socially valuable software: a community could collectively buy out a program's source and be certain the code is actually delivered once funding settles.
key_works: Witness-conditioned release and private smart contracts.

title: Dormant Institution Capsule — proposal
subfield: Program escrow, succession, and institutional survival
open: Can we construct a "dormant institution capsule" — a self-contained sealed package that preserves an institution's charter, encrypted state, funding rules, and reactivation procedure so it can be faithfully revived after an arbitrarily long dormancy? Formally, the capsule must bundle an executable charter, encrypted state, funding rules, and an authenticated reactivation procedure into a package whose integrity and authenticity survive long-term storage.
status: This is currently only a proposal; no construction exists. Cryptographic longevity, interpreter preservation, and secure migration remain open research obligations. Related foundations come from timed-release encryption and composable protocol design.
solved_when: A concrete construction exists of a sealed package comprising an executable charter, encrypted state, funding rules, and an authenticated reactivation procedure, together with solutions to its identified research obligations: cryptographic longevity, interpreter preservation, and secure migration.
why: It would let long-horizon trusts, observatories, memorial institutions, and intergenerational commitments persist through dormancy and resume operation without relying on continuous human stewardship.
key_works: Timed-release encryption and composable protocol design.

title: Fresh-Work Rental Commons — proposal
open: Can we construct a rental scheme in which a user holds an obfuscated copy of an engine locally, yet each fully specified new job requires a fresh, separately granted permission to run? Formally, the goal is a construction where cached authorized jobs remain executable offline, but no unseen job can be executed without authorization, with secrecy and metering extending to every variable input of the computation.
status: This is a proposal; no construction is given. The envisioned behavior is that cached authorized jobs remain executable while secrecy and metering must cover every variable input to the computation, building on token-based obfuscation and one-time-program limits.
solved_when: A construction exists in which (i) the user possesses the obfuscated engine, (ii) execution of any fully specified new job is gated on separately issued per-job permission, (iii) previously authorized (cached) jobs remain executable, and (iv) secrecy and metering hold for every variable input to the computation.
why: It would enable private local software rentals — the user keeps the obfuscated program locally — with only a small online dependency at each new job, combining offline convenience with per-use control.
key_works: Token-based obfuscation and one-time-program limits.

title: Epoch-Fed Software Appliance — proposal
open: Can we design a distributed software appliance that processes each new data epoch only when the provider supplies a fresh capability for that epoch, so that access to data must be continuously re-granted rather than licensed once?
status: No construction is known; the proposal currently identifies constrained pseudorandom functions and broadcast encryption as the relevant technical tools, and requires that old epochs stay usable while future keys remain underivable from previously distributed capabilities.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each epoch's data can be processed using that epoch's capability alone, old epochs remain usable with their capabilities, and no future epoch's key can be derived from any set of previously distributed capabilities.
why: It would enable rental-style access to continuously changing data feeds, models, and operational environments, where the provider must be able to cut off future access without recalling what has already been delivered.
key_works: Constrained pseudorandom functions and broadcast encryption.

title: Meter of Recognized Work — proposal
open: Can we design a metering scheme in which each newly authorized computation consumes a registered allowance determined by a declared work metric, so that resource use is enforced rather than merely declared?
status: This is currently only a proposal: reservation of allowance does not guarantee delivery, and pricing, cancellation, and fair settlement would each require separate mechanisms. Related boundaries come from Pinocchio and one-time-program techniques.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which every authorized computation provably consumes allowance according to the declared work metric at authorization time.
why: It would enable portable metered software to run across untrusted hosting providers, with usage accounting the host cannot forge or ignore.
key_works: Pinocchio and one-time-program boundaries.

title: Anonymous Software Lending Library — proposal
open: Can a software library issue unlinkable entitlements that let patrons borrow programs up to a bounded number of uses, so that admission, loan quotas, and query authorization compose without enabling linkability or duplicate borrowing?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The requirement is that admission, loan quotas, and query authorization must compose without linkability or duplicate borrowing. Related primitives come from anonymous credentials and token-based obfuscation.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a library allocates a bounded number of prospective software uses through anonymous entitlements, with admission, loan quota enforcement, and query authorization composing correctly while preserving unlinkability and preventing duplicate borrowing by the same patron.
why: It would give public access to expensive software with far stronger patron privacy than conventional licensing allows.
key_works: Anonymous credentials and token-based obfuscation.

title: Clock-Rooted Offline Lease — proposal
open: Can a rented appliance be given a hardware-protected deadline, after which it can no longer authorize fresh inputs even while operating fully offline?
status: Currently a proposal; the mechanism requires a trustworthy monotone clock, and previously issued capabilities and outputs remain reusable after expiration. Hardware-assisted one-time programs establish the relevant extra-resource distinction.
solved_when: A construction exists in which authorization of new inputs provably stops once the protected hardware deadline passes, relying only on a trustworthy monotone clock, while previously issued capabilities and outputs remain reusable offline.
why: It would enable offline rentals whose trust requirements are confined to narrowly scoped trusted hardware, rather than a continuously online authority.
key_works: Hardware-assisted one-time programs establish the relevant extra-resource distinction.

title: Quantum Return-for-Refund Exchange — proposal
open: Can we build a cryptographic leasing scheme in which returning a leased quantum capability provably restores the renter's deposit — i.e., successful return is verifiable and triggers an honest refund? The goal is a construction for a supported function family where lease return, refund, and verifier accountability all hold under quantum-secure assumptions.
status: This is a proposal stage problem. Any realization requires quantum resources, appropriate quantum-secure assumptions, and verifier accountability; the notion does not extend to arbitrary software. Related foundations come from secure software leasing and hidden-coset constructions.
solved_when: A construction exists for a supported (not arbitrary) function family in which a successful lease return entitles the renter to a deposit refund, using quantum resources and quantum-secure assumptions, with verifier accountability.
why: It would give cryptographic lending of selected capabilities with meaningful return semantics, rather than leases that merely expire.
key_works: Secure software leasing and hidden-coset constructions.

title: Declining-Privilege Lease — proposal
open: Design a lease mechanism in which the set of authorized actions shrinks as the lease progresses through epochs — later epochs permit only subsets of the actions available earlier in the lease.
status: The design is at the proposal stage. The central known constraint is that every relevant actuator must enforce current authorization, because archived binaries cannot enforce the reduction themselves. Key works: constrained pseudorandom functions.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a holder of the lease at any epoch can perform exactly the actions authorized for that epoch, with the authorization reduction enforced by every relevant actuator (since archived binaries cannot enforce the reduction themselves).
why: It would serve temporary administrators, emergency operators, and apprentices whose authority should decrease in predetermined steps over the life of the lease.
key_works: Constrained pseudorandom functions.

title: Computational Decommissioning Registry — proposal
open: Can an institution cryptographically demonstrate that a retired software identity has lost all prospective authority — that no new recognized jobs or action privileges can accrue to it? Formally, this asks for a proof mechanism establishing that the identity's permission state has transitioned irreversibly to a revoked, non-issuing mode.
status: The known guarantee concerns prospective authority only; it cannot establish destruction of every binary or historical output. Related work includes private state transitions and the impossibility of software-only consumption.
solved_when: A construction exists by which an institution can produce a verifiable proof that a given software identity will not receive new recognized jobs or action privileges going forward.
why: It enables precise, reviewable retirement of proprietary services and autonomous agents, so that decommissioning is an auditable act rather than an informal promise.
key_works: Private state transitions and the impossibility of software-only consumption.

title: Model Charterworks — proposal
open: Can a deployed AI model ship as a sealed "capsule" that carries verifiable proofs of specified formal properties and emits receipts binding each answer to its committed version? In other words, can proof-carrying code ideas be extended to full model capsules, with the proofs remaining meaningful even when the model's contents must stay confidential under authorized queries?
status: Currently a proposal. What is missing is model-family confidentiality under authorized queries, and neither execution proofs nor indistinguishability obfuscation (iO) establishes general alignment. Key works: zkCNN and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a model capsule (i) carries proofs of its specified formal properties, (ii) produces a receipt for each answer tying it to the committed model version, and (iii) preserves model-family confidentiality under authorized queries.
why: It would enable markets in portable, certified machine capabilities — capabilities that can be bought, sold, and audited without revealing the model or trusting the operator's infrastructure.
key_works: zkCNN and proof-carrying code.

title: Sealed Pluralism Council — proposal
open: Can a council of machine experts release only an aggregate decision — plus selected disagreement indicators — under a public aggregation rule, without any individual member's behavior becoming inferable from repeated outputs? Formally: design sealed council mechanisms where the published aggregate and chosen disagreement signals leak nothing about the individual members' underlying decision functions.
status: It is currently recognized that running separate models does not by itself prove intellectual independence, and that repeated publication of aggregates can reveal individual member behavior. Related technical building blocks exist in multi-input functional encryption and zkCNN, but no sealed council mechanism of the kind described is known.
solved_when: A concrete mechanism exists that (i) publicly aggregates council members' decisions under a fixed public rule, (ii) exposes chosen disagreement indicators, and (iii) provably prevents reconstruction or inference of any individual member's behavior across repeated aggregates.
why: It would enable councils composed of proprietary or culturally distinct machine expertise to act jointly and publicly while protecting each member's internals — mere architectural separation does not confer intellectual independence, and naive repeated aggregation reveals individuals.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and zkCNN.

title: Least-Authority Agent Shell — proposal
open: Can an agent's externally observable actions be confined to an explicit mandate, no matter what its internal planner proposes? Formally, is there a shell construction in which every accepted action provably satisfies the mandate, even when the planner is arbitrary or adversarial?
status: The proposal is currently at the idea stage; the obstacle identified is the need for secure key-use constructions and complete mediation at every relying endpoint. Related foundations come from constrained functions and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A construction exists that achieves complete mediation of every accepted action at every relying endpoint and rests on secure key-use constructions, such that mandate compliance holds regardless of the planner's internal proposals.
why: It would enable confidential agents that operate across untrusted machines under enforceable action limits, rather than relying on trust in the agent's own reasoning.
key_works: Constrained functions and proof-carrying code.

title: Private-Memory Fiduciary — proposal
open: Can a personal AI agent hold its long-term memory in encrypted form and still answer questions, disclosing only what a strict, recipient-specific disclosure function permits? Formally: can an agent's archive be usable solely through committed, recipient-specific disclosure functions, so that no answer channel — natural language included — leaks beyond the policy?
status: Currently, natural-language answers can reveal archive contents; what is missing is a usable, bounded confidentiality model for the disclosure policy. Related work exists in functional encryption and prediction-interface extraction research.
solved_when: A usable, bounded confidentiality model for the disclosure policy exists, with access to the encrypted archive possible only through committed, recipient-specific disclosure functions, and answers (including natural-language ones) provably revealing no archive contents beyond those functions.
why: It would enable portable personal agents whose continuity does not depend on a platform that can read the agent's memory.
key_works: Functional encryption and prediction-interface extraction research.

title: Audit Without Weight Custody — proposal
open: Can an audit institution run registered tests and release certified results from a fixed model version without ever taking custody of the model's weights? More precisely, can such an institution verify reported outcomes against the exact model version under audit while remaining independent of the model's owner?
status: This is currently a proposal; no construction is known. Test representativeness, adaptive benchmark leakage, and training contamination remain separate open questions. zkCNN's inference and declared-dataset accuracy proofs are the closest related work.
solved_when: A protocol exists by which an auditor with no access to weights can run a fixed set of registered tests on a fixed model version and publish certified results that are sound with respect to that exact version.
why: It would enable repeatable audits across competing proprietary models, where weight custody is impossible and self-reported results are unverifiable.
key_works: zkCNN’s inference and declared-dataset accuracy proofs.

title: Sealed-Model Warranty Exchange — proposal
open: Can a model developer sell a genuine warranty on a sealed model's behavior — that is, post collateral against an efficiently checkable formal claim about a specified model and input domain, such that the warranty pays out when the claim fails?
status: Currently only a proposal; it requires meaningful formal promises and a sound connection between the warranted and deployed implementations. Key works include zkCNN, verifiable computation, and private contracts.
solved_when: A scheme exists in which a developer posts collateral backing an efficiently checkable claim about a specified model over a specified input domain, the check meaningfully captures the promised formal property, and the warranted artifact is soundly connected to the deployed implementation.
why: It would make warranties for concrete machine behavior purchasable, giving buyers recourse grounded in verifiable properties rather than trust.
key_works: zkCNN, verifiable computation, and private contracts.

title: Sealed Forensic Replay Laboratory — proposal
open: Can a sealed "replay laboratory" be built that lets investigators obtain certified answers to predefined questions about a recorded execution of an automated system, without trusting the operator of the replay?
status: Complete recording and carefully specified causal questions are considered essential; replay alone cannot establish real-world causation. Related machinery exists in verifiable computation and secret-model inference proofs, but no such laboratory is realized.
solved_when: A recorded execution can be supplied together with a mechanism that returns certified answers to a predefined question set — certification being verifiable by a third party — so that reproducible forensic investigation of the record is possible.
why: It would enable narrow, reproducible investigations of disputed automated actions, replacing reliance on the operator's own account of what their system did.
key_works: Verifiable computation and secret-model inference proofs.

title: Model-Graft Licensing Chamber — proposal
open: Can a composite model be made to enforce the use conditions and revenue rights that each contributor declared, so that no party can extract or exercise a contributor's expertise outside the licensed terms? Formally, this asks for a composition and leakage theorem covering correlated modules and adaptive downstream wrappers built atop them.
status: Currently only a proposal; no composition or leakage theorem exists. Correlated modules and adaptive downstream wrappers are identified as the obstacles requiring new machinery. Related building blocks are multi-input functional encryption and zkCNN.
solved_when: A construction and proof exist in which a composite model built from independently contributed modules provably respects every contributor's declared use conditions and revenue rights — including when modules are correlated and downstream wrappers adapt — with leakage and revenue accounting bounded by the theorem.
why: It would enable locally executable combinations of independently owned machine expertise, letting parties compose licensed model components without a trusted central authority mediating every use.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and zkCNN.

title: Laboratory Inside a Paper — proposal
open: Can a scientific paper be published as a self-contained computational service, so that any reader can run registered analyses against authenticated inputs and receive results that are both reproducible and accompanied by proofs of correct execution?
status: Current state of the art draws on reusable garbled circuits and verifiable computation, but reproducible execution alone does not establish valid methodology, and broad query access may allow reconstruction of protected components.
solved_when: A reader can execute any registered analysis on authenticated inputs and obtain reproducible, proof-bearing results, without the authors' continued involvement.
why: It would yield reproducible scientific services that keep running independently of their authors, making published methodology executable and verifiable rather than merely described.
key_works: Reusable garbled circuits and verifiable computation.

title: Negative-Result Vault — proposal
open: Can competing laboratories share a cooperative memory of costly experimental failures without leaking each other's research programs? Formally, is there a protocol by which a researcher can query whether a proposed experiment falls into a registered failure class and receive an authorized yes/no warning, while a query policy prevents reconstruction of any competitor's registered program?
status: A proposal only; no construction exists. It would likely build on functional encryption, and the open obstacles are trustworthy record-keeping and a query policy that prevents reconstruction of competitors' research programs.
solved_when: A deployable vault construction exists: records of failure classes that are trustworthy, a query mechanism returning authorized warnings about overlap, and a proven query policy under which queries cannot be used to reconstruct competitors' research programs.
why: Without it, laboratories repeat expensive failed experiments in isolation; with it, a field-level memory of negative results could be shared safely even among rivals.
key_works: Functional encryption.

title: Blind Reproducibility Clearinghouse — proposal
open: Can a set of laboratories, each holding a confidential dataset, jointly learn whether their registered analyses agree under a declared criterion — without any party seeing another's data or intermediate results?
status: This is a proposal; the agreement metrics, measurement authenticity, and information leakage through repeated comparisons still need specification. Multi-input functional encryption is noted as a key relevant technique.
solved_when: A clearinghouse protocol is fully specified in which participating laboratories register analyses against confidential datasets and learn only whether a declared agreement criterion is met; the protocol's agreement metrics, guarantees of measurement authenticity, and resistance to information leakage through repeated comparisons are all formally defined.
why: It would enable replication studies across confidential industrial and academic datasets that cannot be shared directly, extending reproducibility checking to settings where raw data must stay private.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption.

title: Double-Sealed Benchmark Arena — proposal
open: Can we build a benchmark arena in which solvers commit to their solutions before seeing the tasks, tasks are kept hidden from them, and the scores are computed without either side learning more than the outcome — all through a tournament interface that runs in a bounded number of rounds? Formally, this asks for a two-party evaluation protocol with function privacy for the benchmark and data privacy for the solver, where the host cannot adaptively extract information from repeated scoring.
status: The proposal is at the requirements stage: the two core needs are two-sided function-and-data privacy and explicit controls on adaptive score leakage. Candidate building blocks noted are multi-input functional encryption and reusable garbled circuits.
solved_when: A working tournament protocol exists that simultaneously guarantees function privacy for the hidden benchmark tasks and data privacy for the committed solver submissions, with explicit, proven controls limiting what an adaptive host can learn about submissions from repeated score queries — the "double-sealed" property — within a bounded round budget.
why: It would allow persistent, repeated evaluations of solvers without requiring trust in the benchmark host, removing the need for a trusted third party who could otherwise leak tasks or submissions.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and reusable garbled circuits.

title: Executable Preregistration — proposal
open: Can research conclusions be made to provably follow an analysis procedure that was committed to in advance, without revealing the full method at commitment time — an "executable preregistration" whose designated properties were certified before the data were touched?
status: No working mechanism exists yet; data selection and omitted experiments can still distort conclusions, and the registration boundary remains to be made explicit. Related ideas come from proof-carrying code and hidden mechanisms.
solved_when: A mechanism exists by which a researcher commits to an analysis procedure, obtains advance certification of its designated properties, and later produces results that verifiably follow that committed procedure, with an explicit registration boundary that rules out distortion through data selection or omitted experiments.
why: It would enable preregistered industrial research while avoiding premature disclosure of the complete method — letting firms commit to honesty without giving away their secrets.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and hidden mechanisms.

title: Privacy-Budget Observatory — proposal
open: Can a public-interest statistical observatory be built so that every newly authorized answer draws down a globally registered privacy allowance, enforced across all evaluator replicas rather than per-server goodwill? Formally, this asks for a distributed privacy-budget accounting mechanism that remains sound under retries, correlated queries, and authorizations issued by multiple parties.
status: This is a proposal; what is required — a formal privacy accountant and a proof covering retries, correlated queries, and distributed authorizations — is not yet in hand. Related foundations come from randomized functional encryption and differential privacy.
solved_when: A formal privacy accountant exists together with a proof that budget accounting covers retries, correlated queries, and distributed authorizations across all replicas — no authorized answer can be produced without consuming registered allowance.
why: It would allow durable observatories that answer public-interest statistical questions without any permanently trusted operator who can read the raw data.
key_works: Randomized functional encryption and differential privacy.

title: Embargoed Discovery Exchange — proposal
