open: Can a market be designed in which a seller of a secret method or dataset proves its value through certified answers to buyer-chosen queries, under a negotiated evaluation allowance, without revealing the underlying asset?
status: It is currently recognized that evaluation outputs can substitute for the asset itself; pricing, query selection, and release fairness still require joint analysis. Related primitives include hidden mechanisms and functional encryption.
solved_when: A joint analysis of pricing, query selection, and release fairness exists for such an exchange, showing when evaluation outputs can substitute for full disclosure of the asset.
why: It would enable markets for discoveries that can demonstrate value without immediately publishing the full result.
key_works: Hidden mechanisms and functional encryption.

title: Field-Evidence Bounty Engine — proposal
open: Can we design an engine in which a contribution automatically earns a bounty once authenticated evidence of it satisfies a pre-registered acceptance predicate — with no discretionary judgment at payout time? Formally, this asks for a measurement and attestation model in which cryptographic authentication of records and computation suffices to check the predicate.
status: Cryptography can authenticate records and computation (publicly verifiable computation), but trustworthy observation still requires a measurement and attestation model that does not yet exist.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a contribution's evidence can be authenticated and checked against a registered acceptance predicate, triggering the bounty without any discretionary reviewing office.
why: It would enable distributed collection of valuable observations, replacing a centralized reviewing office with verifiable evidence.
key_works: Publicly verifiable computation.

title: Winner-Only Electoral Authority — proposal
open: Can an electoral authority, holding a finalized set of encrypted ballots, publish nothing beyond the prescribed winner and its verification evidence — while still allowing anyone to independently check the count? Formally, design an election scheme whose public output is exactly the winner plus a proof, with all other ballot information hidden.
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. Coercion, ballot inclusion, endpoint compromise, and repeated-election inference currently require separate guarantees. Related directions come from functional encryption and coercion-resistant election research.
solved_when: A scheme exists in which the public transcript of a finalized encrypted ballot set consists solely of the declared winner and its verification evidence, enabling independent counting, with separate guarantees in place for coercion resistance, ballot inclusion, endpoint compromise, and repeated-election inference.
why: It would enable elections with independently runnable counting and a deliberately narrow public result, exposing nothing about non-winning choices or voting patterns.
key_works: Functional encryption and coercion-resistant election research.

title: Executable Electoral Mandate — proposal
open: Can a delegation mechanism be built in which a representative program casts votes that are automatically recognized as valid only when they fall within the mandate its voters committed to? Formally, this asks for "executable" mandates: vote authority constrained by committed policy, enforced as a property of the voting system itself.
status: This is currently only a proposal; its semantics and receipt-freeness need careful treatment, and a programmable mandate could itself facilitate coercive arrangements. Related thinking appears in constrained-capability and Dark DAO research.
solved_when: A semantics for programmable mandates is defined in which proposal handling and receipt-freeness are rigorously treated, and votes outside the committed mandate are not recognized — while the mechanism does not open new coercive arrangements (e.g., Dark DAO–style attacks).
why: It would give delegation that stays conditional through leadership changes and organizational conflict, rather than granting unconditional authority once a representative is chosen.
key_works: Constrained capabilities and Dark DAO research.

title: Census Across Private Ontologies — proposal
open: Can a set of institutions, each holding its own private ontology of categories, jointly compute answers to agreed aggregate questions — such as census tabulations — without ever publishing the mappings between their local category systems? More precisely: is there a protocol in which translations among private ontologies remain hidden while the public learns only the agreed aggregate outputs?
status: Translation legitimacy, duplicate enrollment, and inference from small populations remain substantive open problems. Key works relevant to the setting are multi-input functional encryption and differential privacy.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which institutions compute agreed public aggregates over their private category systems with no individual mapping between ontologies ever revealed, and with documented handling of duplicate enrollment and inference risks from small populations.
why: It would enable cross-community censuses that produce aggregates in terms locally meaningful to each community, rather than forcing a single imposed category scheme on all participants.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and differential privacy.

title: One-Person Entitlement Gate — proposal
open: Can we build a system that issues each qualifying person at most one recognized entitlement within a specified domain, without relying on a trusted party to track identities? Formally, the goal is a credential mechanism — in the spirit of Camenisch–Lysyanskaya anonymous credentials — that is Sybil-resistant yet guarantees one-person-one-entitlement across the domain.
status: Human uniqueness still lacks a credible enrollment system; obfuscation alone does not solve Sybil resistance from nothing. Camenisch–Lysyanskaya anonymous credentials provide the relevant building block for anonymous issuance.
solved_when: A construction exists in which every qualifying person obtains at most one recognized entitlement in the specified domain, even against adversaries creating multiple pseudonymous enrollments.
why: It would enable private distribution of civic benefits and participation rights — benefits could be claimed anonymously without anyone being able to double-dip or be excluded.
key_works: Camenisch–Lysyanskaya anonymous credentials.

title: Membership Compatibility Passport — proposal
open: Can an applicant cryptographically prove that their existing confidential affiliations are compatible with a prospective institution's committed rules, without revealing the affiliations themselves? More precisely: is there a protocol ensuring the proof remains sound even when some affiliations are undisclosed and the institution receives many compatibility queries over time?
status: This is currently a proposal; no construction is known. The envisioned building blocks are multi-input functional encryption and anonymous credentials. The main identified obstacles are that missing affiliations and repeated compatibility queries can undermine the promised guarantee.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which an applicant demonstrates compatibility between confidential existing affiliations and an institution's publicly committed rules, and the guarantee is formally shown to withstand both withheld affiliations and repeated compatibility queries.
why: It would let individuals join institutions and collective-choice processes without routinely disclosing complete affiliation histories, which today forces an all-or-nothing tradeoff between privacy and participation.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and anonymous credentials.

title: Association Without a Readable Roster — proposal
open: Can an organization broadcast authorized messages and capabilities to its registered members without ever materializing a readable roster of who belongs? Formally, is there a private recipient-selection procedure that delivers only to enrolled members while hiding the membership list even from the delivery mechanism and from later compromise of accumulated credentials?
status: This is a proposal-stage problem. The suggested technical route is iO-based private broadcast encryption. No analysis of enrollment, delivery metadata, or compromise of accumulated credentials has yet been carried out.
solved_when: A construction exists in which enrollment, delivery metadata, and the accumulated credentials upon later compromise are all analyzed and shown not to reveal the membership roster, while authorized members still receive messages and capabilities.
why: It would allow durable associations to coordinate and distribute capabilities with sharply reduced exposure of their collective membership, protecting members from retribution or surveillance if any party's records are seized.
key_works: iO-based private broadcast encryption.

title: Private Civic Lottery — proposal
open: Can a lottery be run so that participants' privacy is protected while the public still receives convincing invitations and certificates proving the selected sample satisfies a published sampling rule?
status: This is a proposal stage problem; the record notes only that enrollment quality, nonresponse, and selective-abort bias must be handled explicitly, with randomized functional encryption suggested as a relevant technique.
solved_when: A scheme exists that simultaneously preserves participant privacy and produces publicly verifiable certificates that the drawn sample conforms to the published sampling rule, with enrollment quality, nonresponse, and selective-abort bias handled explicitly.
why: It would enable private sortition for citizens' panels, oversight bodies, and public-service opportunities without exposing who was in the eligible pool or who responded.
key_works: Randomized functional encryption.

title: Conscience Accommodation Allocator — proposal
open: Can we design a scheduler that honors workers' certified private constraints — religious observances, medical needs, conscientious objections — while learning nothing beyond the accommodations actually assigned and a bounded amount of feasibility information? Formally: is there a mechanism that computes a valid schedule under certified private constraints, revealing only the assigned accommodations plus leakage bounded in advance?
status: Open as a proposal. The known obstacles are twofold: preferences can be strategically reported, so participants may misstate constraints to game outcomes, and repeated scheduling interactions may leak enough feasibility information to reveal the hidden constraints over time. Related directions include hidden mechanisms and multi-input functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction (or impossibility result) exists for a scheduler that respects all certified private constraints and whose output reveals only the assigned accommodations together with feasibility information bounded by an explicitly stated budget.
why: It would let workplaces and civic institutions accommodate private convictions without building a catalog of them — the institution schedules around what it must, but cannot mine or reconstruct the hidden constraints themselves.
key_works: Hidden mechanisms and multi-input functional encryption.

title: Bargaining Delegate With a Private Reservation — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can a software delegate bargain on a person's behalf across many counterparties without leaking that person's private reservation value through the sequence of offers it accepts or counters? Formally, is there a bargaining interface in which the delegate commits to a private preference schedule and the information revealed about reservation values through offer probing is quantifiably bounded?
status: Offer probing can reveal reservation values, and the bargaining interface needs a quantified leakage model; a proposal drawing on hidden mechanism design.
solved_when: A bargaining protocol is given in which a delegate accepting or countering authenticated offers according to a committed private preference schedule provably bounds leakage of the reservation value, with the bound made explicit under a quantified leakage model.
why: It would enable persistent individual representation across many counterparties — a delegate that can negotiate repeatedly without its acceptance pattern becoming a probing oracle for its principal's willingness to pay.
key_works: Hidden mechanism design.

title: Secret-Skill Guild — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can a guild of independently owned computational skills be organized so that clients invoke any member's method through a single governed interface, while each provider's proprietary technique stays hidden? Formally: construct a protocol in which multiple parties contribute protected skill modules, and arbitrary client queries are answered correctly without revealing the modules' internals or breaking accountability for who contributed what.
status: Open problems remain around correlated skill outputs and malicious module composition, which require confidentiality and provenance proofs; candidate tools include reusable garbled circuits and functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which (i) skill modules remain confidential against clients and other members, (ii) composed or malicious modules cannot corrupt outputs or provenance undetected, and (iii) provenance proofs tie each output to its contributing module — with security proofs for confidentiality and provenance under the model adopted.
why: It would let cooperative professional infrastructure run on independently owned methods: practitioners could pool expertise into a shared service without surrendering their proprietary techniques or anonymity of contribution.
key_works: Reusable garbled circuits and functional encryption.

title: Tender Examiner Without a Hiring Insider — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can a selection process commit, before reviewing any submissions, to a procedure that later reveals only the award decision and specified feedback derived from a finalized applicant set — without anyone acting as a trusted hiring insider with full access to the work?
status: This is a proposal; scoring validity and the disclosure needed for meaningful applicant challenge remain open design questions. Related techniques come from hidden mechanism design and private verifiable computation.
solved_when: A committed selection mechanism is specified that releases the award and the stipulated feedback from the finalized applicant set, and its scoring validity and the sufficiency of its disclosure for meaningful applicant challenge are established.
why: It would enable portable hiring and commissioning processes in which no party needs discretionary access to submitted work, protecting applicants while preserving contestability.
key_works: Hidden mechanism design and private verifiable computation.

title: Portable Professional Practice — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can a licensed professional capsule — a narrow expert function packaged for execution — be made to carry its professional authority with it, so that it operates on sensitive data wherever that data resides, while all use and disclosure constraints remain externally auditable? Formally, this asks for a construction of a constrained functional object whose permitted behavior and disclosure boundaries are enforceable and verifiable by third parties.
status: The method's output interface may permit reconstruction of restricted information, and professional adequacy is not established by execution integrity alone; no construction currently satisfies both requirements. Key works: token-based obfuscation and constrained functions.
solved_when: A construction exists that both (i) prevents reconstruction of restricted information through the capsule's output interface, and (ii) establishes professional adequacy — not merely execution integrity — under its auditable use and disclosure constraints.
why: Expertise that can travel to sensitive data instead of requiring data to travel to its owner, enabling licensed professional functions (legal, medical, financial) to operate under confidentiality regimes that forbid data movement.
key_works: Token-based obfuscation and constrained functions.

title: Wage Bond With an Executable Acceptance Rule — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can a labor-market escrow contract pay a worker automatically when their deliverable passes a registered, machine-checkable acceptance test — and can such a test be made to genuinely capture the promised work while resisting parties who probe it adaptively to game acceptance?
status: This is a proposal; the central open issues identified are that the acceptance test must capture the promised work and that private tests need protection against adaptive probing. Key works: verifiable computation and Hawk.
solved_when: A wage-bond construction exists in which escrowed compensation is released exactly when the deliverable satisfies the registered machine-checkable conditions, the acceptance test faithfully captures the promised work, and private tests are protected against adaptive probing.
why: It would allow contract work to be paid on objectively verifiable performance, reducing dependence on a client's later discretion over whether the work is accepted.
key_works: Verifiable computation and Hawk.

title: Collective Exit Trigger — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can a group of workers commit to a collective action — such as a coordinated exit — through an institution that announces the decision only once the number of authenticated private commitments crosses a registered threshold? Formally, the design should aggregate authenticated private inputs into a single revealed trigger whenever the threshold is met, without any party learning individual commitments below that point.
status: Coercion, membership legitimacy, and suppression of submissions remain outside the threshold calculation. Candidate building blocks are multi-input functional encryption and anonymous credentials.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which an institution's announcement is released if and only if authenticated private commitments satisfy the registered threshold, with no individual commitment exposed below that threshold.
why: It enables coordinated bargaining with less dependence on a central organizer who reads the full roster of who has signed on, reducing the organizer's power to coerce or suppress.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and anonymous credentials.

title: Grievance-to-Repair Covenant — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can an organization credibly bind itself to specified changes once an authenticated aggregate grievance condition is met — that is, can the trigger, the verification, and the commitment be made binding without relying on management's goodwill?
status: Classification quality, false submissions, and protection of small groups remain unguaranteed and require explicit guarantees; candidate technical foundations come from randomized functional encryption and differential privacy.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which an authenticated aggregate grievance condition, once met, mechanically forces the specified organizational changes, with explicit guarantees on classification quality, bounded false submissions, and protection of small groups.
why: It would give feedback systems real consequences rather than ones contingent entirely on management discretion, so grievances translate into repair rather than optional response.
key_works: Randomized functional encryption and differential privacy.

title: Executable Apprenticeship — proposal
subfield: Labor, professions, and markets for expertise
open: Can we design an apprenticeship structure in which a learner progresses through a committed capability curriculum with certified prerequisites, such that the progression is executable — guided access, assessment, and eventual ownership of selected capabilities?
status: The current articulation notes that assessment must distinguish competence from answer sharing, and that anything deliberately taught becomes reusable knowledge; no construction or result yet exists. Related ideas draw on constrained functions and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: A curriculum design exists in which each stage's prerequisites are certified, the learner's competence is distinguished from answer sharing in assessment, and deliberately taught capabilities become reusable knowledge owned by the learner at completion.
why: It enables apprenticeships that verifiably transfer capability rather than mere answers, combining guided access, assessment, and eventual ownership of selected capabilities.
key_works: Constrained functions and proof-carrying code.

title: Treaty Interpreter With Private Doctrines — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can a jointly committed institution determine the treaty actions its parties must take, while proving to all participants that its determination complies with the public agreement — even though the reasoning it relies on involves ambiguous language, disputed facts, and inferences about private red lines? Formally: construct a treaty-interpreter mechanism that takes public and private inputs and outputs specified actions together with a proof of compliance with the public treaty text.
status: This is a proposal. The need for explicit treatment of ambiguous language, disputed facts, and inference about private red lines is identified; candidate machinery comes from multi-input functional encryption and hidden mechanisms. No construction is known.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a jointly committed institution outputs the specified treaty actions and produces a verifiable proof that these actions comply with the public agreement, while handling ambiguous language, disputed facts, and inference about private red lines explicitly rather than leaving them implicit.
why: It would allow continuous treaty administration without a universally trusted interpretive office, replacing that trust with verifiable machinery.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and hidden mechanisms.

title: Local-View Ceasefire Scheduler — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can parties who distrust each other jointly schedule a ceasefire while each learns only the pieces of the schedule assigned to them? Formally, is there a scheduler that satisfies all registered separation and timing constraints yet reveals to each party only its designated local assignments?
status: Ground conditions, communications availability, and inference from observed movement remain external limitations; relevant machinery comes from multi-input functional encryption and private computation.
solved_when: A construction exists that, given arbitrary registered separation and timing constraints, produces a schedule satisfying them while provably revealing to each participant nothing beyond its designated local assignments.
why: It would enable coordination in settings where full operational transparency would itself obstruct agreement, since revealing the whole plan leaks capabilities or intentions that no side will expose.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and private computation.

title: Reciprocal Compliance Escrow — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can a program be designed that executes a specified reciprocal exchange — for example, the mutual release of commitments under a treaty or reconciliation agreement — without either party ever holding unilateral control over the release condition? More precisely, is there a mechanism that realizes fair delivery, resolvable evidence disputes, and non-selective abort without relying on code obfuscation?
status: The proposal is at the idea stage. Fair delivery, evidence disputes, and selective abort are known to require mechanisms beyond obfuscation; related machinery exists in Hawk and general secure multiparty computation, but no construction for this reciprocal-compliance escrow setting is known.
solved_when: A concrete construction is given in which neither party can unilaterally trigger, withhold, or selectively abort the release condition of the reciprocal exchange, with fair delivery and evidence-dispute resolution handled by the mechanism itself rather than by obfuscation.
why: It would let treaty stages and reconciliation agreements proceed with far less dependence on a discretionary intermediary, removing the trusted third party as a bottleneck and source of bias.
key_works: Hawk and general secure multiparty computation.

title: Reconciliation Match Without a Matchmaker — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: A private matching institution releases contact capabilities only when both parties’ committed conditions are satisfied.
status: Matching queries can become identity probes; consent withdrawal applies only to future introductions.
why: Voluntary reconciliation systems that do not create a readable central relationship archive.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption.

title: Historical Truth Predicate Trust — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can mutually distrusting parties obtain certified answers to questions phrased in an agreed predicate language over authenticated confidential records, without exposing the records themselves? Formally, this asks for a mechanism combining verification of archival authenticity with computation on encrypted or constrained-access data so that only the predicate's answer is revealed.
status: No mechanism is known that meets the full goal. Archive completeness and authenticity are currently handled separately from computation, and existing approaches leave a concrete weakness: repeated predicate evaluations may allow reconstruction of the sensitive records. Related directions come from functional encryption and constrained access.
solved_when: Parties with no mutual trust can evaluate any predicate in the agreed language over the archive, receiving a certified answer while the underlying confidential records remain unrevealed — in particular, repeated evaluations of different predicates do not allow reconstruction of the sensitive records.
why: It would open a middle path between total archival closure and unrestricted publication, letting parties use sensitive evidence as grounds for cooperation without surrendering it.
key_works: Functional encryption and constrained access.

title: Corridor Through Hidden Red Lines — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can mutually distrustful parties jointly establish a passage through contested territory when each refuses to reveal its full set of constraints? Formally, devise a mechanism by which a planner publishes a corridor that provably satisfies every party's committed constraints and the public humanitarian requirements, without any party disclosing more than the corridor itself reveals.
status: Repeated route requests are known to reveal constraints, but safe operation still depends on truthful and current physical information. Related key works concern multi-input functional encryption and hidden mechanisms.
solved_when: A construction exists in which repeated route requests reveal only the constraints they must, and the agreed corridor is released satisfying all committed constraints and public humanitarian requirements, with safe operation depending only on truthful and current physical information.
why: It enables practical agreements among parties unwilling to disclose their entire constraint map, such as humanitarian corridors negotiated under distrust.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption and hidden mechanisms.

title: Reciprocal Inspection Capsule — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can an inspection instrument be built so that it releases only the single agreed-upon property of its authenticated measurements, and nothing else about what it observed?
status: No construction is known. The main obstacles identified are measurement authenticity, instrument calibration, and concealed bypasses, each of which requires independent physical assurance beyond purely cryptographic means. Related technical directions include functional encryption and verifiable computation.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the instrument's output provably leaks no more than the agreed property, with authenticity of measurements, calibration guarantees, and resistance to concealed bypasses established by independent physical assurance.
why: It would enable reusable inspection arrangements between distrusting parties while minimizing confidential operational disclosure — inspectees could be verified without exposing sensitive details of their operations.
key_works: Functional encryption and verifiable computation.

title: Sanctuary Continuity Trust — proposal
subfield: Diplomacy, peace, and cooperation under distrust
open: Can a designated successor be granted the narrow ability to perform specific future services on behalf of a sanctuary — such as issuing credentials or continuing an arrangement — without ever being able to read the underlying archive of beneficiary records? Formally, this asks for a cryptographic succession mechanism in which delegated capabilities are functional and revocable-in-effect for new uses, yet the sensitive dossier itself is never transferred or exposed.
status: No security model currently exists for succession or adaptive compromise in this setting; once information has been exposed it cannot be recalled, and both succession and adaptive compromise remain in need of explicit formal treatment. Related primitives come from functional encryption and private broadcast encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which an authorized successor can execute only the specified future service capabilities, and can learn nothing beyond them about the beneficiary archive; previously disclosed information is treated as unrecoverable, so the guarantee must hold for all future interactions following succession.
why: It would allow confidential services to survive a change of operator — continuity of care or protection — without handing over an entire sensitive dossier, so trust in a successor can be scoped rather than all-or-nothing.
key_works: Functional encryption and private broadcast encryption.

title: Confidential Clinical Method Cooperative — proposal
open: Can a licensed evaluator run a confidential clinical method on protected patient inputs and return clinician-directed outputs, together with verifiable receipts attesting to which method version was used and that it executed faithfully?
status: Existing directions include secret-model inference proofs and functional encryption; however, clinical validity and meaningful safety specifications require evidence beyond faithful model execution.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a licensed evaluator processes protected patient inputs locally, produces outputs usable by clinicians, and emits version and execution receipts — while the method owner never receives the patient records.
why: It would enable clinically usable computation on patient data without transferring records to the method owner, keeping sensitive care information under local control.
key_works: Secret-model inference proofs and functional encryption.

title: Minimum-Necessary Emergency Record — proposal
open: Can we build a patient-defined disclosure policy that releases the minimum necessary medical information only when presented with verifiable emergency credentials? Formally, a mechanism that grants narrow, function-specific access to records conditioned on a qualifying emergency credential, without exposing anything beyond the policy's scope.
status: A proposal stage; the areas of emergency authenticity, clinical question semantics, and coercive access requests still need explicit governance. The underlying technique envisioned is function-specific disclosure through functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which disclosures are limited to the minimum necessary for the emergency credential presented, governed by explicit rules covering emergency authenticity, clinical question semantics, and coercive access requests.
why: It shrinks the disclosure surface during emergencies, so urgent care access no longer requires opening the entire record.
key_works: Function-specific disclosure through functional encryption.

title: Genomic Kinship Covenant — proposal
open: Can related participants — family members whose genomes overlap — jointly authorize computations on their encrypted genetic records, releasing only the predicates they have collectively agreed to disclose?
status: Open proposal. The core difficulty is that genetic information concerns multiple people at once: repeated query outputs and inferences implicating nonparticipants complicate any workable privacy definition. Multi-input functional encryption is the relevant primitive.
solved_when: A mechanism exists whereby multiple related participants authorize specific joint predicates over encrypted genetic records, with a privacy definition that handles repeated outputs and implications for nonparticipants.
why: It would enable shared biological services — such as familial risk screening — with negotiated, enforceable boundaries around family information.
key_works: Multi-input functional encryption.

title: Trial Amendment Guardian — proposal
open: Can we build a system that automatically checks any proposed amendment to a research protocol against each participant's committed consent constraints and the public procedural requirements, so that no amendment takes effect unless it provably respects them?
status: This is a proposal only; no construction exists. A known limitation is that consent language must map to meaningful computable predicates, and a proof cannot resolve every clinical judgment. Key works: proof-carrying code and hidden mechanisms.
solved_when: Every proposed protocol amendment is verified against each participant's committed consent constraints and the applicable public procedural requirements before taking effect, with consent language expressed as meaningful computable predicates.
why: It gives executable continuity of consent: participants' original commitments remain enforced as research protocols change, rather than relying on manual review that may miss violations.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and hidden mechanisms.

title: Adverse-Event Sentinel Commons — proposal
open: Can a persistent institution be constructed that continuously issues registered statistical alerts over adverse-event data contributed by many organizations, without ever gaining plaintext access to that data?
status: This is a proposal; no design exists yet. Data quality, multiple testing, false alerts, and disclosure accounting all need validation. Key works: randomized functional encryption and differential privacy.
solved_when: A working design for such a sentinel commons exists in which data quality, multiple-testing control, false-alert rates, and disclosure accounting are all validated over encrypted contributed event data.
why: It would enable cross-institution surveillance of potential care failures while granting far narrower access to the underlying data than today's models require.
key_works: Randomized functional encryption and differential privacy.

title: Inherited Care Archive — proposal
open: Design a scheme in which a claimant's credential chain determines which narrowly defined familial disclosures about inherited care information are permitted. Formally, the system should combine verifiable credential provenance with a consent interpretation process so that access is gated by provenance and recorded historical consent rather than by biological ancestry alone.
status: Existing cryptographic tools — anonymous credentials and functional encryption — prove credential provenance, but not biological ancestry by itself, and historical consent requires a defined interpretation process; no construction combining these for familial disclosures is known.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a claimant presenting a valid credential chain can obtain exactly the disclosures permitted under narrowly defined familial rules — no more — with cryptographic proof of credential provenance and a specified interpretation process for historical consent.
why: It would enable sharing of intergenerational care information across a family while preserving selective family privacy for each individual in the chain.
key_works: Anonymous credentials and functional encryption.

title: Patient-Paced Disclosure Covenant — proposal
open: Can a personal disclosure program enforce a patient's explicit preferences about who may see their information, in what staged sequence, and within which authorized clinical contexts? Formally, this asks for a mechanism by which disclosures are governed by machine-readable preference rules covering audience, staging, and clinical context.
status: This is a proposal; preference revision, urgent exceptions, and the meaning of disclosure categories are identified as needing careful specification. Key works referenced include functional encryption and constrained capabilities.
solved_when: A working specification and construction exist in which a patient's stated preferences about audience, staging, and authorized clinical context are enforced on every disclosure, including specified behavior for preference revision and urgent exceptions, with well-defined semantics for disclosure categories.
why: It would give patients portable, inspectable information preferences that carry across care institutions, rather than consent decisions that must be renegotiated at every provider.
key_works: Functional encryption and constrained capabilities.

title: Biological Sample Permission Exchange — proposal
open: Can we construct an exchange mechanism in which biological samples are released only to assays whose capabilities provably satisfy the contributor's committed conditions and compensation schedule?
status: Enforcement currently depends on controlled instruments and custody; an independent physical analysis cannot be prevented by software. Related ideas appear in constrained functions and hidden mechanism design.
solved_when: A construction exists in which every registered assay must demonstrate capabilities meeting the contributor's committed conditions and compensation schedule before receiving access, with authorized uses auditable.
why: It would enable negotiable biological research permissions with auditable authorized uses, giving contributors enforceable control over how their samples are used and compensated.
key_works: Constrained functions and hidden mechanism design.

title: Secret-Heart Art Dynasty — proposal
open: Can a committed generative art identity be designed so that authorized encounters reveal only selected branches of its expression tree while the underlying seed remains secret?
status: Currently a proposal only: the construction requires a seed-confidentiality analysis, revealed works remain copyable, and uniqueness would need a separate registry. Related primitives come from punctured programs and constrained pseudorandom functions.
solved_when: A construction exists in which authorized openings expose chosen branches of the committed generative identity, a seed-confidentiality analysis establishes that the seed is not recoverable from any authorized set of revelations, and uniqueness of revealed works is handled (e.g., by a registry).
why: It enables collectible generative art whose future expressions remain partly undiscovered even as past works are revealed and traded.
key_works: Punctured programs and constrained pseudorandom functions.

title: Private Myth Engine — proposal
open: Can a distributed narrative institution keep its internal state secret while revealing only the story consequences authorized by its registered interaction history?
status: Adaptive play currently teaches the rules, but the desired secrecy has no formal, deliberately limited exploration model; the proposal draws on token-based obfuscation and private state computation.
solved_when: A formal, deliberately limited exploration model exists in which participants who learn the rules through adaptive play cannot recover secrets beyond the story consequences the interaction history authorizes.
why: It would enable persistent fictional worlds whose secrets are discoverable through play rather than readable from source, changing how such worlds can be authored and maintained.
key_works: Token-based obfuscation and private state computation.

title: Branch-Remembering Heirloom — proposal
open: Can a digital heirloom be designed so that every future response it produces provably descends from a single authenticated sequence of its prior choices?
status: The registry establishes recognized continuity, but copied binaries and unofficial alternative histories remain possible; related limits appear in Zexe and one-time-program work.
solved_when: A construction exists in which responses can only be generated by descending from one authenticated lineage of prior choices, with copied binaries and unofficial alternative histories unable to produce recognized responses.
why: It would give digital heirlooms verifiable biographies while keeping their future reactions concealed, something current continuity registries cannot ensure.
key_works: Zexe and one-time-program limits.

title: Unspoiled Puzzle Sanctuary — proposal
open: Can we construct a long-lived public puzzle whose successive disclosures are released automatically — without any discretionary puzzle master — by requiring a qualifying solution witness to activate the next permitted disclosure under an immutable challenge structure?
status: Low-entropy answers remain enumerable, and witness-gated confidentiality is currently only a proposal: it lacks a concrete reduction for the chosen challenge family. Related ideas appear in punctured programs and witness-conditioned cryptography.
solved_when: A concrete reduction is given for a chosen challenge family, showing that witness-gated confidentiality holds even though low-entropy answers remain enumerable, with the disclosure sequence fixed immutably in advance.
why: It would enable public mysteries that persist and unfold over long horizons without trusting a human curator to decide when to reveal the next secret.
key_works: Punctured programs and witness-conditioned cryptography.

title: Secret-Genome Art Breeding — proposal
open: Can a child's protected parameters be derived from committed parent parameters under an agreed recombination rule, without revealing the parents' secrets?
status: This is currently a proposal; no construction is known. Many descendants may reveal parent traits, and adaptive related-output confidentiality needs a dedicated theorem. Related cryptographic machinery appears in multi-input and randomized functional encryption.
solved_when: A scheme exists in which committed parent parameters can be recombined into a child whose protected parameters are correctly derived under the agreed rule, together with a theorem proving adaptive related-output confidentiality — i.e., that many descendants do not reveal parent traits.
why: It enables markets and games built around private, verifiable digital lineages, where participants must prove a child's lineage without exposing their secret traits.
key_works: Multi-input and randomized functional encryption.

title: Event-Changed Monument — proposal
open: Can we construct a digital "monument" whose state evolves through certified events such that, once an event is recorded in its canonical history, the monument's official successor state can never revert to the earlier branch?
status: The proposal builds on ideas of private state transitions and software-copyability limits; permanence is currently understood as belonging to recognized state, with earlier recordings and copied versions unable to be destroyed cryptographically.
solved_when: A construction exists in which any recognized, certified event entering the canonical history makes return to the prior branch impossible, while permanence attaches to recognized state — earlier recordings and copied versions remain cryptographically indestructible but non-canonical.
why: It would enable digital memorials and civic artworks whose consequential histories cannot be rewritten, giving their evolving states a genuine, enforced sense of institutional permanence.
key_works: Private state transitions and software-copyability limits.

title: Consent-Bound Memorial — proposal
open: Can a digital memorial be constructed that answers only the questions permitted by its owner's committed audience and subject rules, even as repeated queries accumulate? Formally, is there a scheme where semantic consent boundaries and cumulative answer leakage admit a bounded, revisable interpretation model?
status: No construction exists yet; the problem remains at the proposal stage. The required semantic consent boundaries and cumulative answer leakage currently lack a bounded, revisable interpretation model. Related techniques come from functional encryption and secret-model execution proofs.
solved_when: A memorial object exists that provably enforces the owner's committed audience and subject rules, with a bounded and revisable model controlling cumulative answer leakage across queries.
why: It would allow inheritable relationships with an archive — ongoing access for designated parties — without unrestricted posthumous exposure of the deceased's secrets.
key_works: Functional encryption and secret-model execution proofs.

title: Lottery of Unopened Worlds — proposal
open: Can one construct a cryptographic scheme in which a scarce authorization token permits its holder to select and reveal exactly one branch from a committed collection of concealed narrative branches? Formally, this asks for a composition of choice enforcement with one-time-style authorization over hidden alternatives.
status: Currently a proposal only. Known obstacles: the scheme appears to require quantum resources and lacks a composition theorem for choice enforcement; the opened world, once revealed, remains copyable. Related primitives include hidden-coset tokenized signatures and one-time programs.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a single authorization deterministically yields access to exactly one committed branch, with security proved via a composition theorem for choice enforcement.
why: It would enable art whose consequence — which world gets opened, and that no other can be — is cryptographically enforced rather than socially promised.
key_works: Hidden-coset tokenized signatures and one-time programs.

title: Public Secret-Compiler Notary — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: Can a distributed ceremony produce an executable together with a source commitment and a correctness certificate, while preserving the agreed confidentiality threshold?
status: Currently, selective abort, biased retries, adaptive corruption, and compiler side channels each lack a unified treatment. Key works: secure multiparty computation and punctured programs.
solved_when: A ceremony is specified that outputs an executable, source commitment, and correctness certificate and provably preserves the agreed confidentiality threshold against selective abort, biased retries, adaptive corruption, and compiler side channels in a unified treatment.
why: It would give credible founding ceremonies for institutions designed to have no privileged internal reader.
key_works: Secure multiparty computation and punctured programs.

title: Constitutional Type Registrar — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: Can a capsule be granted an institutional type only upon demonstrating, to any verifier, compliance with a published interface and authority specification — so that authority to act is established by proof rather than trust?
status: Open as a proposal; the requirement is expressive types that remain auditable and compose across independently governed systems. Related groundwork includes proof-carrying code and Raziel.
solved_when: A capsule that proves compliance with a public interface and authority specification receives its institutional type, with the proof checkable across independently governed systems.
why: It would make institutional software interoperable while keeping authority boundaries machine-checkable, rather than enforced by ad hoc trust assumptions.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and Raziel.

title: Cross-Capsule Leakage Clearinghouse — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: When should a request to disclose information about an obfuscated institution be granted? Specifically, when does combining the requested disclosure with all previously registered disclosures still respect a declared leakage contract?
status: No such theorem is known; the central missing result is compositional confidentiality for the chosen descriptor language and adversarial auxiliary information. Related foundations come from universal composability and differential-privacy composition.
solved_when: A compositional confidentiality theorem holds for the chosen descriptor language and adversarial auxiliary information: any admitted disclosure request is provably compatible, under composition with registered prior disclosures, with the declared leakage contract.
why: It would give privacy commitments that survive ecosystems of interacting services rather than holding only for each service in isolation.
key_works: Universal composability and differential-privacy composition.

title: Behavioral Equivalence Registry — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: When are two committed capsules interchangeable — that is, when do they implement the same confidential institutional commitment for a specified interface and state relation?
status: General equivalence is computationally difficult; the useful frontier is expressive restricted languages with obtainable certificates. Related work includes iO's equivalence definition and proof-carrying code.
solved_when: An equivalence notion is defined for a restricted yet expressive capsule language, together with an obtainable certificate (in the proof-carrying sense) that two given capsules are equivalent for the specified interface and state relation.
why: It would let competing implementers of the same confidential institutional commitment demonstrate interchangeability, enabling competition among implementers without revealing the commitment itself.
key_works: iO’s equivalence definition and proof-carrying code.

title: Sealed-Capability Provenance Chamber — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: Can a tracing institution take a recovered (possibly pirated) evaluator and credibly attribute it to the specific capability issuance that produced it, under a precisely stated tracing guarantee — even when the underlying programs are obfuscated?
status: Generic perfectly functionality-preserving watermarking conflicts with indistinguishability obfuscation, so the scope of tracing and the permissible functional deviations are the crux of any viable design. Related prior work includes Nishimaki–Wichs watermarking and iO-based traitor tracing.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a tracing institution, given a recovered evaluator, identifies the registered issuance responsible, with the tracing guarantee and any permissible functional deviations explicitly stated and proved.
why: It would enable accountable distribution of protected methods and institutional credentials: leaks of obfuscated evaluators could be traced back to the issuance event that authorized them.
key_works: Nishimaki–Wichs watermarking and iO-based traitor tracing.

title: Cryptographic Bankruptcy Receiver — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: Can we build a "cryptographic bankruptcy receiver": a mechanism by which an obfuscated organization, upon registered dissolution, distributes its assets and prospective powers according to a priority rule it committed to in advance?
status: This is a proposal only; no construction exists. The outstanding obstacles identified are that claim completeness, external assets, and cross-system revocation require shared recognition and dispute procedures. Related primitives come from Zexe, Hawk, and functional encryption.
solved_when: A registered dissolution provably distributes assets and prospective powers according to the committed priority rule, with mechanisms covering claim completeness, external assets, and cross-system revocation via shared recognition and dispute procedures.
why: It enables orderly dissolution of organizations whose principal assets are protected computational powers, rather than leaving those powers orphaned or contestable.
key_works: Zexe, Hawk, and functional encryption.

title: Private Mutual-Recognition Embassy — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: Can confidential institutions recognize and act on each other's authority without ever revealing their internal trust structures? Formally, can a cross-institution action be authorized only when both parties simultaneously prove compatible credentials, mandates, and disclosure conditions, under composable recognition rules?
status: This is a proposal-level open problem. What is missing are composable recognition rules, revocation semantics, and protection against correlated credential disclosures. Related technical building blocks exist in work on iO-based multiparty key exchange and private broadcast encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which mutual recognition composes across institutions, revocation semantics are well-defined, and correlated credential disclosures across institutions cannot be used to break privacy — i.e., the interaction reveals nothing beyond the accept/reject of the joint condition.
why: It would let federations of confidential organizations cooperate — sharing authority and triggering joint actions — without merging their internal trust structures or exposing their governance to each other.
key_works: iO-based multiparty key exchange and private broadcast encryption.

title: Obfuscation Continuity Endowment — proposal
subfield: Institutions that govern other obfuscated institutions
open: Can an endowment be constructed that funds certified migration of an obfuscated institution to new implementations, while provably preserving its specified rights, state relationships, and disclosure boundaries? Formally, the endowment must guarantee that each migration preserves the institution's security and functional properties across implementation changes.
status: Migration must occur before the old protection fails; practical classical indistinguishability obfuscation does not automatically supply post-quantum security.
solved_when: A construction exists in which migration completes before the old protection fails, with the endowment certifying preservation of rights, state relationships, and disclosure boundaries through each migration, including resilience to changes in cryptographic assumptions such as the transition to post-quantum security.
why: It enables institutions designed to outlive compiler obsolescence and shifts in cryptographic assumptions, rather than collapsing when their underlying obfuscation technology becomes insecure.
key_works: Assumption-based iO constructions and composable protocol design.
